title: A reserve in the body
hook: A body material can affect how easily an animal stays afloat.

doesNotKnow: Some sharks have a large oil-rich liver. How can the oil contribute to buoyancy?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: Some sharks have a large oil-rich liver. How can the oil contribute to buoyancy?

claims.text: Some sharks have a large oil-rich liver. How can the oil contribute to buoyancy? The cutaway highlights oil within a shark liver. Oil is less dense than water and an oil-rich liver can contribute to buoyancy. The diagram isolates one contributor; it does not show the contributions of fins, motion or the rest of the body.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, fish anatomy and behavior, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
Which tissue in some sharks can contribute oil that helps with buoyancy? An oil-rich liver is one contributor to buoyancy in some sharks.
